title: helm: introduce cost-profiles chart with QuantConfig CRD and exporter
author: Marcus Li
description: Motivation: Provide a Helm-native way to ship operator-friendly defaults for batching, cache presets, and quantization profiles so platform deployers can opt into cost-optimization automation during chart install/upgrade. This PR adds a new 'cost-profiles' Helm chart that bundles a QuantConfig CRD, a lightweight exporter sidecar that emits curated presets to the control-plane API, and opinionated values for batching/caching defaults. Key features: 1) QuantConfig CRD: a cluster-scoped CRD model that encodes quantization tiers (fp16, int8, q4_0), acceptable accuracy degradation thresholds, and rollout tags; 2) exporter: a small Deployment (exporter sidecar) that reads installed CR instances and posts signed preset bundles to the Redwood control plane or dumps them to a configured S3 bucket; 3) values.yaml presets: safe-by-default batch sizes, KV cache TTLs, and host-level annotations to opt deployments into conservative or aggressive profiles; 4) upgrade path: chart registers/validates existing QuantConfig objects and runs a dry-run export during helm upgrade by default. Backwards compatibility: existing clusters that don't install this chart will be unaffected; the CRD is optional and installs as an opt-in. Security: exporter uses ephemeral service account with RBAC limited to reading the CRD and writing to a configured outbound endpoint; TLS and token-auth are enforced. Testing: unit templates tested via helm unittest; end-to-end smoke tests run in the staging cluster to ensure installer doesn't change existing deployments; we exercised the exporter against a local mock control-plane and an S3 sink; load tests verified default batch sizes do not increase median latency beyond the 95th-percent SLO for small models. Checklist: - [x] Add Chart scaffolding + README - [x] Implement QuantConfig CRD template and validation schema - [x] Add exporter manifest + ConfigMap-driven templates - [x] Values presets + examples for conservative/aggressive modes - [x] Unit tests (helm-unittest) - [x] E2E smoke in staging - [x] Security review and RBAC policy - [x] Docs entry and upgrade notes How to test locally: helm install ./cost-profiles --set exporter.sink=mock --namespace redwood-test; verify crd present with kubectl get quantconfigs.redwood.ai; create a QuantConfig and watch exporter logs. Release notes: Adds cost-profiles Helm chart that enables cluster operators to export curated batching/caching defaults and quantization presets to the Redwood control plane; opt-in CRD and exporter; no automatic application of presets to runtime without explicit operator approval. Migration notes: None required for existing installs; operators who adopt should review preset thresholds in values.yaml. Related: ENG-3421 (helm presets design), ENG-4277 (quant profile schema).

review_comments: Ava Chen: Nice enclosure of the CRD and the exporter. Please reduce the default 'aggressive' batch size for seq_len>512 as we've seen SLO regressions in perf-canary; also add a guard in the exporter to avoid repeated POSTs on transient network flaps.
Marcus Li: Thanks Ava — lowered aggressive default for seq_len>512 from 64 to 32 and added exponential backoff to the exporter retry loop (configurable in values.yaml).
Diego Morales: RBAC LGTM but can we scope the Role to the chart namespace instead of cluster-wide? If the exporter only needs to read the CRD in the same namespace, that'd be better for security.
Marcus Li: Updated role to namespace scope and adjusted exporter to watch namespace-local CR instances; documented the change in README and upgrade notes.
Priya Nair: Can you add a helm test that creates a QuantConfig and asserts the exporter emits a valid JSON bundle to a local file sink? That would catch templating regressions.
Marcus Li: Added helm test that runs a lightweight mock file sink in a Job and validates the bundle; included tests in CI matrix.
